name: Rupee Rewind gold 1991: Chatterbox dramatic (heart_plain ref, exaggeration 0.7, cfg 0.3), script rewritten

lines.text: Gold just hit a one-year low, only days before Dhanteras.
But in nineteen ninety-one, India had to pawn its own gold, just to pay its bills.
Rewind to nineteen ninety-one. India is running out of dollars.
What's left pays for just a few weeks of imports.
If the dollars run out, India defaults.
First, twenty tonnes of gold seized from smugglers is sold, with a promise to buy it back.
That brings in about two hundred million dollars. It is not enough.
So the RBI pledges forty-seven tonnes of its own gold, with the Bank of England and the Bank of Japan.
The gold leaves the country, as a guarantee.
In return, India gets about four hundred million dollars in loans.
It is a pawn shop, for an entire country.
That July, the rupee is cut in value, and India starts opening up its economy.
In twenty twenty-four, the RBI moved about a hundred tonnes of its gold from the UK, back to India.
So gold isn't just jewellery. In a crisis, you can borrow against it.
But the real lesson? Keep cash for emergencies, so you never have to pawn the gold.
And for India, it all began with the dollars running out.
